```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

rNest estimates the nesting chronology of birds, the dates when a nest was
started and when the young left it, from a few visits to the nest. From these
dates, it describes the breeding phenology of a set of nests: the share of
nests that are active on each day of the season.

```{r}
library(rNest)
```

## Nest observations and nesting parameters

rNest needs two tables. The first one holds the observations: one row per
visit to a nest, with the nest id, the species (4-letter AOU code), the date,
and the number of eggs and young seen. `nestwatch` is a small excerpt from the
Project NestWatch database:

```{r}
data(nestwatch)
nestwatch[1:5, c("nest_id", "species_code", "date", "eggs", "young")]
```

The second one gives the nesting parameters of each species: clutch size,
length of laying, incubation and rearing, etc. `nestingparameters` holds them
for the species in `nestwatch`:

```{r}
data(nestingparameters)
nestingparameters[, c("species_code", "clutch", "laying", "incub", "rearing")]
```

## The chronology of one nest

`chronology()` estimates the chronology of a single nest. Its first two values
are the estimated initiation date (first egg) and fledging date:

```{r}
nest <- nestwatch[nestwatch$nest_id == 43359, ]
chronology(nest, nparam = nestingparameters)[1:2]
```

## Many nests at once

`active.nest()` does the same for every nest in a table. Nests can be
selected by species (`sp`), year (`year`) or region (`layer`, `region`):

```{r}
nests <- active.nest(nestwatch, nparam = nestingparameters, progress = FALSE)
nests[, c("sp", "id", "initiation", "fledging", "warning")]
```

Nests without eggs or young get no dates, and `warning` says why.

## Breeding phenology

`nesting.activity()` turns these dates into the proportion of nests active on
each day, here by species. The first row gives the number of nests used:

```{r, results = "hide"}
activity <- nesting.activity(nests)
```

```{r}
activity[c(1, 40:45), ]
```

Use `by = "year"` or `by = "region"` to group nests by year or region instead.

`nesting.calendar()` draws these proportions as a calendar:

```{r, include = FALSE}
# nesting.calendar() opens its own plot device, which knitr can't capture:
# draw it into a png file and include that file below.
calendar_png <- knitr::fig_path("png")
dir.create(dirname(calendar_png), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
old <- options(device = function(width, height, ...) {
  png(calendar_png, width = width, height = height, units = "in", res = 96)
})
```

```{r, results = "hide"}
nesting.calendar(activity)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
invisible(dev.off())
options(old)
knitr::include_graphics(calendar_png)
```

## The interface

`rNest()` opens the rNest user interface (`rNid()` opens it in French). It
gives access to the same tools with menus and maps, and adds nesting calendars
predicted by ecodistrict across Canada.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
rNest()
```
